contracts.contract_plain_english: For the unshifted basic algorithm, each positive exponential is computed with relative error at most u and the computed terms are then summed recursively. contracts.contract_plain_english: For the basic unshifted softmax algorithm, each numerator exponential has relative error at most u, the recursively summed denominator has first-order relative error at most (n+1)u, and the final division contributes another error at most u. Their composition gives relative error at most (n+3)u + O(u^2) in every component, then the same coefficient in the relative infinity-norm bound of Theorem 3.3. The result excludes overflow and underflow and inherits the assumed accuracy of exp. [PDF p. 6, anchor: Algorithm 3.1 and standing assumption; PDF p. 8, anchor: componentwise derivation following equation (3.5); PDF p. 9, anchor: Theorem 3.3, equation (3.6)]

contracts.contract_plain_english: Subtracting one common real shift from every logit leaves every exact softmax component unchanged: g_j is exp(x_j-a) divided by the sum of all exp(x_i-a). Consequently, the exact components sum to 1. The paper uses deviation from this invariant to compare computed fp16 softmax vectors and reports that the alternative formulations look less accurate, but it gives no normalization-error theorem and does not claim that floating-point sums equal 1 exactly.
